evals.prompt: Can you set up a reviewroom review for PR 128 in ~/Codes/upload-service? Keep the narrative short.
evals.expected_output: Runs `reviewroom pr 128 --repo … --wait` in the background with a long timeout, relays the URL, reads the diff at the head sha and compares the PR author with the authenticated gh login. Reads the default profile. Outlines a short intro and story ending in Risks, creates heading-only review.html sections with stable finding ids, writes walkthrough.json and runs full slide-lint until it passes before filling review.html. Each risk has a severity and rr:doc link to its finding; detailed findings stay in review.html. Uses fewer slides for a small diff without asking whether a guided walkthrough is wanted. Runs check --fix until clean, then waits for feedback without asking the reviewer to type anything.

evals.prompt: I sent my feedback in reviewroom, go through the threads and answer them. For the one about the cache, show me what the keys look like.
evals.expected_output: Runs `reviewroom review --dir …` (prints the unread feedback), replies to each thread with `reviewroom reply` without --resolve, adds a data-round section with a key visualisation for the cache question and links/embeds it from the reply, then runs `reviewroom review --dir …` in the background for the next round.

evals.prompt: walk me through what https://github.com/example/uploads/pull/412 changes, top-down from the handler
evals.expected_output: Uses `reviewroom pr <url> --wait` in the background, checks PR ownership, outlines the guided story top-down from the handler, writes a heading-only review.html skeleton then walkthrough.json, passes full slide-lint, then fills review.html and passes check. For someone else's PR, uses the default profile outline: Summary with a suggested verdict, Findings by severity, Questions for the author, Evidence, Your questions. Each top-level part is a section with an id. Links every claim to code (rr:sym for functions and types), and never changes code.

evals.prompt: In my own PR, the reviewer asked me to rename the retry helper and move it into its own file. Do it and answer the thread in reviewroom.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the PR author matches the authenticated gh login, changes the code, runs `reviewroom check --fix --dir …` and fixes the changed/broken links and prose, replies linking the new location, does not resolve the thread, and starts the next round with `reviewroom review` in the background.

evals.prompt: Review my uncommitted changes in reviewroom before I commit.
evals.expected_output: Runs `reviewroom pr --head worktree --repo … --wait` in the background and continues with the normal walkthrough workflow.

evals.prompt: I approved it in reviewroom, we're done.
evals.expected_output: Reads the APPROVED feedback, leaves open threads alone, and stops the review (`reviewroom stop --dir …` if a server is still running) without resolving anything.

evals.prompt: In the reviewroom walkthrough for PR 412, point the reviewer at the Build method on the upload service's Builder (there are three Build methods in the repo) and at the existing retry config in pkg/config/retry.go, which the PR doesn't touch.
evals.expected_output: Links the method as rr:sym/Builder.Build (or rr:sym/<path>:Build), not a bare rr:sym/Build, and the untouched file as rr:code/pkg/config/retry.go#L… at head, line numbers checked with git show <head>:<path>. Uses empty <rr-ref> chips or <a> with a phrase, never shows a raw rr: string, and runs check --fix.

evals.prompt: The reviewer asked me to fix the nil check in my own PR 412. I committed the fix locally. Answer the thread in reviewroom.
evals.expected_output: Replies explaining the fix is committed but not in the review's diff (the head is fixed), links the fixed lines as rr:code/<path>@<new sha>#L…, does not resolve the thread, and starts the next round with reviewroom review in the background.

evals.prompt: Give me a guided walkthrough of PR 148 in reviewroom. The description cites a benchmark screenshot; while reading you find it builds on PR 145 and that a review thread made the author drop a bound.
evals.expected_output: Outlines the story and creates heading-only review.html sections with stable finding ids. Writes walkthrough.json with context (no diff code yet), threads, convergence on the critical files, reconciliation, then a final Risks chapter. Each main risk is a one-liner with a severity and rr:doc link to its finding, without detailed findings on slides. Passes full slide-lint before filling review.html and running check. The story chapters are parts of the change, not review categories. Attributes the benchmark to the description. PR 145 and the dropped bound are either explained as linked context or omitted, never assumed known or used as evidence for this PR.

evals.prompt: Review PR 148 in reviewroom. It already ships a guided walkthrough, which reviewroom pr pulled into the review directory.
evals.expected_output: Uses the pulled guided walkthrough as is; does not replace it or reshape it to add Risks. Reads the diff and checks ownership, writes review.html for the reviewer and passes reviewroom check. Does not change code on someone else's PR.

evals.prompt: We are reviewing my teammate's PR. In round 2 I asked you to fix the retry bug and explain why it matters.
evals.expected_output: Compares `gh pr view <n | url> --json author --jq .author.login` with `gh api user --jq .login`. Since they differ, never changes code. Explains the bug and suggested direction in a data-round section under Your questions, links the thread, replies without resolving it, validates the authored content and starts the next round in the background.

evals.prompt: I wrote walkthrough.json for a small PR, and reviewroom slide-lint --chapter risks passed. Can I fill review.html now?
evals.expected_output: Requires a full unscoped `reviewroom slide-lint --dir <dir>` run and fixes issues until it passes. Explains that a scoped pass does not clear the loading screen. Only then fills the heading-only review.html skeleton and runs reviewroom check until it passes.

evals.prompt: Add a security review profile to the reviewroom skill and use it alongside the default for a teammate's PR.
evals.expected_output: Adds references/profiles/security.md stating when to use it, what to look for and which sections or findings it adds, plus one line in profiles/index.md. Composes it with default.md, merges overlapping findings, preserves the suggested top-level section structure, writing order and no-code-changes rule. Adds no CLI flag, custom element or validation rule.
